profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest-speedup workload of the round (0.510) and the mid-size 16-bit regime with the highest measured per-block overhead; primary evidence for the scalar/MTE2 split.
Highest-latency workload (1.075ms) and representative of the large 16-bit regime where MTE2 is most loaded; also the shape that gained most from round 1 (+140% speedup).
Distinct fp32 regime at the largest shape; needed to separate a cube-bound case from the 16-bit memory/overlap cases before recommending one change.

Best-case control (1.142, the only 16-bit shape above parity) and the smallest grid; used to test whether the winning regime has the same or a different limit, and it exposed the 9-block under-occupancy.
Second-worst speedup (0.554) at 1024^3 - a boundary shape between the scalar-bound small regime and the MTE2-bound large regime, and the shape with the largest scalar/MAC imbalance.

findings.label: 16-bit 2048^3/4096^3: MTE2 is the busiest AIC unit but is no longer saturated, so the load path is latency- rather than bandwidth-limited
findings.backend_detail: Ascend910B4-1 (dav-c220-cube), 20 AI cores, CANN 9.0.0, triton 3.5.1/flagtree 0.6.0, kernel launched as MIX_AIC with Block Num 256 / Mix Block Num 512 at 2048^3
findings.inference: Widening BLOCK_K to 512 removed the round-1 MTE2 serialization (ratio 0.97 -> 0.63 at 2048^3), but MTE2 still idles 17-37% of AIC time while the cube is only 43-57% busy, and msprof reports every AIC/AIV memory pipe below 80% of peak bandwidth while active. The per-K-fragment load (128x512 fp16 = 256KB, ~1.85us per fragment at ~138GB/s per core) is the longest single stage of each block, yet with num_stages=2 and only 4-8 fragments per block the load latency is not fully hidden: the block wall time is ~12us AIC-busy plus ~2us of exposed AIV tail, not a throughput ceiling. This means further K-widening alone should not be expected to move geo_mean much; the remaining gain is in overlap/latency, not in raw load bandwidth.

findings.label: AIC scalar/address-issue pipe is the busiest AIC unit at the short-K shapes (384^3, 1024^3) and is a co-dominant cost at 2048^3
findings.backend_detail: scalar = AIC scalar/issue pipe (aic_scalar_*); no SASS-equivalent mapping available because level=instruction timed out
findings.inference: At 1024^3 the scalar/address-issue pipe is busy 24.5us versus 10.6us of cube MAC (2.3x), and at 384^3 it is 5.9us versus 1.0us (5.9x); these are exactly the shapes whose speedups are weakest/least improvable (0.554 at 1024^3) or least parallel (384^3). Scalar busy time exceeds MAC time in absolute terms even at 2048^3 (76.4us vs 66.5us). With BLOCK_M=BLOCK_N=128 the K loop has only 2 iterations at 1024^3 and 4 at 2048^3, so per-fragment index arithmetic, mask/pointer updates and pipeline bookkeeping are amortized over very little work, and each block carries a K-independent cost. A per-block time fit (2048^3 and 4096^3) gives ~7.9us fixed + ~1.58us per 128x512 fragment, which also reproduces the measured 1024^3 latency (4 waves x ~11us = 43.4us), i.e. about half of the mid-size block time is overhead that neither the cube nor the load pipe performs. This is an issue/overlap cost, not a bandwidth cost; the instruction-level listing that could name the dominant scalar opcodes could not be collected (simulator deadline expired), so the split between loop control, address generation and set/wait-flag bookkeeping remains unproven.

findings.label: 384^3 uses only 9 of 20 AI cores and 1024^3 runs 3.2 waves, so tile granularity leaves the device partly idle on exactly the latency-critical shapes
findings.backend_detail: no direct occupancy metric in msprof output; block counts from op_summary and device core count from the service target description (20 AI cores)
findings.inference: The 128x128 tile yields a 3x3 grid at 384^3 and an 8x8 grid at 1024^3. Against the 20 AI cores reported for npu:0, 384^3 can occupy at most 9 cores (<=45% of the device, cube_utilization 30.7%) and 1024^3 needs 3.2 waves, so its last wave is only 20% occupied (216 of 1280 possible core-slots idle) - hence cube_utilization 66.8%. Because ~7.9us per block is K-independent (finding 2), this coarse granularity is charged in full on each under-filled wave. This is inference from block counts plus core count, not a direct occupancy counter.

findings.label: fp32 4096^3 is a distinct cube-bound regime (MAC 0.83, cube utilization 94%) and should not be targeted by the same fix
findings.backend_detail: fp32 path uses BLOCK_K=256, num_stages=2; 1024 blocks over 20 cores
findings.inference: For fp32 the cube is already the pacing unit (2097us of MAC in 2523us of AIC time, scalar only 0.169, MTE2 0.530) and cube utilization is 94%, so unlike the 16-bit shapes there is little scheduling headroom left; the remaining gap to the reference (2.62ms vs 2.27ms, speedup 0.868) reflects cube instruction throughput at BLOCK_K=256 (fp32 cannot compile BLOCK_K=512). Optimization effort should stay on the 16-bit mid/large shapes where the same tile leaves pipes at 0.43-0.63 utilisation.

findings.label: The AIV epilogue tail is exposed: aiv_time exceeds aicore_time at every profiled shape while AIV pipes are ~90% idle
findings.backend_detail: MIX_AIC task: AIC (cube) and AIV (vector) sub-kernels per block; AIV performs bias add, ReLU and store of the tile
findings.inference: In the MIX_AIC launch the vector side consistently finishes 10-20% later than the cube side (179.9 vs 155.9us at 2048^3, 1046.6 vs 952.8us at 4096^3, 44.9 vs 35.8us at 1024^3, 8.95 vs 7.29us at 384^3, 2622.7 vs 2522.9us fp32) while its own pipes are only ~6-12% busy, so it is dependency-blocked on AIC results and its per-block bias+ReLU+store tail is the last un-overlapped stage of each block. That tail, plus pipeline fill/drain, is the K-independent part of the ~7.9us per-block cost and is therefore not addressable by widening BLOCK_K; a scheduling/pipelining change is the plausible lever.

performance_interpretation: Round-2 metrics profiling (msprof, level=metrics) was collected on 5 timing workloads of the passing eval snapshot and confirms that the round-1 MTE2/widened-BLOCK_K direction worked but is now largely harvested. The single kernel mba_gemm_kernel (MIX_AIC) shows no saturated pipe at any profiled shape: at 2048^3 fp16 the busiest AIC unit is MTE2 at 0.627 while the cube MAC sits at 0.433 and the scalar pipe at 0.496 (aic_mte2_ratio dropped from 0.97 in round 1); at 4096^3 fp16 MTE2 rises to 0.825 with MAC at 0.566; the vendor's own post-profile summary for this kernel states that aicore MTE1/MTE2/MTE3 and aivector MTE2/MTE3 bandwidth utilization are all below 80% when active and aivector compute usage below 20%. At the two worst-speedup shapes the cost picture changes regime: at 1024^3 fp16 (speedup 0.554) the top AIC unit is the scalar/address-issue pipe (24.49us = 0.685 of aicore time, versus 10.56us MAC), and at 384^3 fp16 (the only shape above 1.0x) scalar is 5.94us = 0.814 versus 1.01us MAC, with only 9 of the 20 AI cores occupied. Fitting per-block time across K (2048^3: ~14.2us/block over 4 K-iterations; 4096^3: ~20.5us/block over 8 K-iterations) gives a K-independent per-block cost of ~7.9us plus ~1.58us per 128x512 K-fragment; that model reproduces the 1024^3 (64 blocks, 4 waves, 43.4us) and 384^3 measurements, so roughly half of the mid-size kernel time is per-block overhead (pipeline fill/drain, scalar bookkeeping, and an AIV epilogue tail) rather than memory throughput. fp32 4096^3 is a genuinely different, cube-bound regime (aic_mac_ratio 0.831, cube_utilization 94.0%), so the headline geo_mean deficit is not explained by one mechanism.

next_experiment.action_description: In mba_gemm_kernel, raise NUM_STAGES from 2 to 4 while holding the resident L1/UB footprint constant by halving BLOCK_K: 2-byte dtypes BLOCK_K=256 (BLOCK_M=BLOCK_N=128 unchanged), fp32 BLOCK_K=128. This converts pipeline width into pipeline depth at equal buffer cost (4 x 128KB vs 2 x 256KB per stage) so more load latency is hidden behind the cube. Evaluate exactly this one variant; do not also change the tile or the epilogue in the same round.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the residual loss is exposed load latency (MTE2 busy only 0.627 at 2048^3 and 0.825 at 4096^3 while MAC is 0.433/0.566 and every memory pipe is below 80% of peak when active), the deeper pipeline should raise aic_mac_ratio and cube_utilization at 1024^3/2048^3 (currently 66.8%/82.0%) and cut the per-block stall, lifting headline geo_mean above 0.6969 with the largest latency gains expected on float16/bfloat16 ::2 (1024^3, 0.0434ms) and ::3 (2048^3, 0.1849ms).
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Risk: a deeper pipeline increases prologue length and per-iteration set/wait bookkeeping, and the scalar pipe is already the busiest AIC unit at 384^3/1024^3 (0.814/0.685) - if the true limit is scalar issue rather than load latency this variant regresses, which is itself the falsification signal. Halving BLOCK_K also partially reverts the round-1 win (BK=256/ns=2 lost to BK=512/ns=2), so the result must be judged against the round-2 baseline geo_mean, not against round 1. UB/L1 compile failure at 4 stages is possible; if the kernel does not compile or correctness fails, revert. Rollback: restore BLOCK_K=512 / NUM_STAGES=2 (the round-2 kernel) unchanged.
success_criteria: Full formal eval of the new candidate returns PASSED with all 27 workloads correct (18 flaggems correctness cases plus 9 timing cases, all dtypes).
Headline geo_mean strictly exceeds the round-2 value 0.6968777786945584.
No workload regresses by more than 3% in latency versus round 2 (in particular float16::0/float32::0 stay at or above their round-2 speedups).

A confirming msprof metrics re-profile of float16::3 shows cube_utilization_pct > 82.0 and aic_mac_ratio > 0.4331 with aic_mte2_ratio <= 0.85, and float16::2 latency < 0.043376 ms; if latent improvement is absent while MTE2 stays < 0.85, the load-latency explanation is falsified and the next round should target the scalar/issue path instead.

msprof timing is diagnostic and does not replace eval latency; all speedup/latency values reported here are the authoritative eval values from get_profile_context.
The 384^3 core-occupancy conclusion uses the service-reported 20 AI cores for npu:0; msprof does not emit a direct occupancy counter.
The per-block fixed/marginal cost split (~7.9us + 1.58us per fragment) is a two-point fit and is only corroborated, not proven, by the 1024^3 and 384^3 measurements.
open_questions: Which AIC scalar/issue opcodes dominate (loop control, address generation, or set/wait-flag pipeline bookkeeping)? The level=instruction run could not deliver a listing: both attempts failed with 'profiling deadline expired during Ascend simulator kernel 0' (profile ids 29a0bb7f005d4a10b22443b423853346 and b09fecdf5dde49d0be8db526a7bdb967) and must be retried, possibly on a single small workload.

Is the ~7.9us K-independent per-block cost dominated by the pipeline prologue (first load latency), the FFTS cross-core handoff, or the AIV epilogue drain? A K-sweep at fixed tile (K=512..4096) would separate fixed from marginal cost directly.
Does NUM_STAGES>2 compile within the UB/L1 budget at BLOCK_K=256 (equal 512KB footprint) on this flagtree build, and does it actually shorten the per-block stall?

Why is 4096^3 fp16 (MTE2 0.825) better in speedup than 2048^3 fp16 (MTE2 0.627)? This is not consistent with pure load-bandwidth scaling and points at the per-block fixed cost / wave granularity rather than at bytes moved.
